faqs.a:
(a)
The hearing shall be conducted by a hearing officer who has been designated by ordinance,
               or in the event that there is no such designation, the city manager or designee shall
               appoint the hearing officer. In the case of a hearing before a board or commission,
               the presiding member of such board or commission shall act as the hearing officer.
               The hearing officer shall have the authority to:
(1)
Schedule hearings and grant such continuances as may be reasonable upon consultation
               with the parties.
(2)
Sign and issue administrative subpoenas, without discrimination between public and
               private parties, requiring the presence of persons and the production of documents
               reasonably necessary to the determination of any issue relevant to the hearing. Subpoenas
               shall be served in the same manner as a subpoena issued by the municipal court. After
               service, copies of subpoenas shall be distributed to the parties. Upon failure of
               any witness to comply with such subpoena, the hearing officer may petition the municipal
               court, setting forth that due notice has been given of the time and place of attendance
               of the witness and the service of the subpoena; in which event, the municipal court,
               after hearing evidence in support of or contrary to the petition, may enter an order
               compelling the witness to attend and testify or produce books, records, or other evidence,
               under penalty of punishment for contempt.
(3)
Administer oaths.
(4)
Rule upon offers of proof.
(5)
Receive evidence.
(6)
Compel testimony.
(7)
Determine all relevant issues of material fact and whether the proposed adverse action
               comports with the requirements of the applicable law.
(8)
Dispose of motions relating to the discovery and production of relevant documents
               and things for inspection, copying, or photographing.
(9)
Regulate the course of the hearing, including setting reasonable time limits on testimony
               or argument and restricting duplicative or irrelevant evidence or testimony.
(10)
Fix the time for filing briefs and other documents.
(11)
Direct the parties to appear and confer to consider simplification of issues, and
               admissions of facts or documents to avoid unnecessary proof or cumulative evidence,
               and limitation of the number of witnesses.
(12)
Issue appropriate orders that control the subsequent course of the proceeding.
(13)
Dispose of motions and procedural matters.
(14)
Control the decorum and conduct of the proceeding, including the reprimanding and
               exclusion from the hearing of any person engaging in improper or inappropriate conduct.
(b)
It shall be unlawful for any person to fail to comply with an order of the hearing
               officer.
(c)
In the absence of objection, the hearing officer may conduct the hearing informally,
               and failure to request any procedure shall constitute a waiver thereof.
(Code 1981, § 2-138; Ord. No. 3608, §§ 1, 2, 4-3-2003)
